added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(d\geq1\), \(\alpha>0\), \(\beta>0\), \(\gamma>\beta\), and \(L\geq4\), and put \(S=\alpha+\beta\).  On \(\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), for every \(n\geq2\), \(h\in(0,1]\), and every admissible projection rank \(k\geq1\), there is a total Borel estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)\), based only on \(O_{1:n}\), such that, with \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}
 \mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau_P(0)\right|
 \leq C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha+
 \sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)}\right\}.
\]
Here admissible ranks form a fixed, geometrically spaced sequence, and every positive real target rank has an admissible rank within a constant factor.  Consequently the last display remains valid, after changing \(C\), for an arbitrary integer tuning target \(k\geq1\).  The estimator uses a one-sided local-polynomial equation, second-order projection corrections to both its matrix and vector moments, the exact Lebesgue projection Gram, singular-value flooring, and clipping; it consists only of sample moments and finite matrix operations.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(D=[0,1]^d\), \(D_h=hD\), and \(K_h(x)=h^{-d}{\bf1}_{D_h}(x)\).  All statements below are uniform over \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\), \(P_X\) is Lebesgue measure on the cube, the observations are i.i.d. by \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), and
\[
 e(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2],\qquad
 e\in\mathcal H_d^\alpha(L/4),\qquad
 \mu_0\in\mathcal H_d^\beta(L),\qquad
 \tau\in\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L).
 \tag{1}
\]
The first equality and interval use \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}shape}\), the definition \(r_0=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\mbox{-}envelope}\); the three smoothness assertions use the corresponding H\"older assumptions in \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\).  The Bernoulli and interiority assumptions imply that every random scalar used below is uniformly bounded.

Let \(m_\gamma=\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), and let \(v:D\to\mathbb R^{q_0}\) be a fixed Lebesgue-orthonormal basis for the polynomials of total degree at most \(m_\gamma\).  Thus \(q_0\) depends only on \((d,\gamma)\) and
\[
 \int_Dv(z)v(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz=I_{q_0}.
 \tag{2}
\]
For a positive integer resolution \(q\), partition \(D\) into \(q^d\) half-open cubes and, on every cube, take all tensor polynomials of degree at least
\[
 p=m_\gamma+\max\{\lceil\alpha\rceil-1,\lceil\beta\rceil-1\}.
\]
Lebesgue orthonormalization gives a vector \(b_k:D\to\mathbb R^k\), where \(k=Mq^d\) and \(M\) is fixed by \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), with the exact, nonrandom Gram
\[
 \Omega_k=\int_D b_k(z)b_k(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz=I_k.
 \tag{3}
\]
These are the admissible ranks.  Their physical mesh is \(h/q=M^{1/d}h k^{-1/d}\), so writing \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\) changes approximation bounds only by a fixed constant.  Taylor's formula on each mesh cube, using exactly the convention \(m=\lceil s\rceil-1\) in the definition of \(\mathcal H_d^s(L)\), gives the following facts.  If \(\Pi_k f=b_k^{\mathsf T}\int_D b_k f\) denotes the exact Lebesgue projection, then for every component \(v_a\),
\[
 \left\|(I-\Pi_k)\{v_a(e(h\,\cdot)-3/8)\}\right\|_2\leq C\ell^\alpha,
 \qquad
 \left\|(I-\Pi_k)\{\mu_0(h\,\cdot)-1/2\}\right\|_2\leq C\ell^\beta.
 \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, on each physical cube, multiply the order-\(\lceil\alpha\rceil-1\) Taylor polynomial of \(e\) by \(v_a\); it belongs to the displayed piecewise-polynomial space and its remainder is at most \(C\ell^\alpha\).  The second inequality is identical with \(\beta\).  Since orthogonal projection minimizes \(L_2(D)\) error, the cellwise bounds imply (4).  This also proves the required approximation property without adding a smoothness assumption on \(\mathbb E[Y\mid X]\).

Define the population local moments
\[
 Q=\int_Dv(z)e(hz)\{1-e(hz)\}v(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz,
 \qquad
 R=\int_Dv(z)e(hz)\{1-e(hz)\}\tau(hz)\,dz,
 \tag{5}
\]
and put \(\theta=Q^{-1}R\) and \(\tau_h(hz)=v(z)^{\mathsf T}\theta\).  These are proof intermediates, not quantities supplied to the estimator.  Equations (1)--(2) give
\[
 \frac3{16}I_{q_0}\preceq Q\preceq\frac14I_{q_0}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Let \(p_\tau\) be the Taylor polynomial of \(\tau\) at zero of degree \(m_\gamma\).  The definition of the H\"older ball gives
\[
 \sup_{z\in D}|\tau(hz)-p_\tau(hz)|\leq Ch^\gamma.
\]
Because \(p_\tau(h\,\cdot)\) lies in the span of \(v\), subtracting its coefficient vector from \(Q^{-1}R\), using (6), and evaluating at \(z=0\) yields
\[
 |\tau_h(0)-\tau(0)|+\sup_{z\in D}|\tau_h(hz)-\tau(hz)|\leq Ch^\gamma.
 \tag{7}
\]
The same argument and \(|\tau|\leq3/4\) show \(\|\theta\|+\sup_D|v^{\mathsf T}\theta|\leq C\).

We now define the estimator explicitly.  Use the deterministic bounded pilots
\[
 \bar e=3/8,
 \qquad
 \bar\mu=1/2.
 \tag{8}
\]
For observation \(i\), let \(z_i=X_i/h\), \(K_i=K_h(X_i)\), \(v_i=v(z_i)\), and \(b_i=b_k(z_i){\bf1}_{D_h}(X_i)\).  Write \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_i f(O_i)\) and \(\mathbb U_n H=\{n(n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}H(O_i,O_j)\).  Set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat Q={}&\mathbb P_n\!left[K_i v_i A_i(A_i-\bar e)v_i^{\mathsf T}\right]\\
 &-\mathbb U_n\!\left[K_iK_jv_i(A_i-\bar e)b_i^{\mathsf T}\Omega_k^{-1}b_jA_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\right],\\
 \widehat R={}&\mathbb P_n\!\left[K_iv_i(Y_i-\bar\mu)(A_i-\bar e)\right]\\
 &-\mathbb U_n\!\left[K_iK_jv_i(A_i-\bar e)b_i^{\mathsf T}\Omega_k^{-1}b_j(Y_j-\bar\mu)\right].
\end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus both \(Q\) and \(R\) receive a localized second-order correction.  The cross-factor \(v_j^{\mathsf T}\) in the correction to \(Q\) is essential: after multiplication by \(\theta\), it produces the projection of \(e\tau_h\).

For a square matrix \(M\), define
\[
 \mathcal J_\lambda(M)=\{\mathfrak f_\lambda(M^{\mathsf T}M)\}^{-1}M^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak f_\lambda(V\operatorname{diag}(s_j^2)V^{\mathsf T})
 =V\operatorname{diag}(\max\{s_j^2,\lambda^2\})V^{\mathsf T},
 \tag{10}
\]
with \(\lambda=1/32\).  This is a continuous, everywhere-defined singular-value flooring map; it equals \(M^{-1}\) whenever the least singular value of \(M\) is at least \(\lambda\).  The announced estimator is
\[
 \widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)
 =\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}
 \left\{v(0)^{\mathsf T}\mathcal J_\lambda(\widehat Q)\widehat R\right\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) are fixed polynomial integrals; (9)--(11) use finite sums and finite matrix operations.  Hence (11) is a total Borel, data-only map even if \(D_h\) contains no observations or \(\widehat Q\) is singular.

We next calculate its bias.  Put \(e^*(z)=e(hz)\), \(\mu_0^*(z)=\mu_0(hz)\), \(\tau^*(z)=\tau(hz)\), \(\Delta_e=e^*-\bar e\), and \(\Delta_0=\mu_0^*-\bar\mu\).  By the Bernoulli regression assumption and iterated expectation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\widehat Q_1
 &=Q+\int_Dv\Delta_e e^*v^{\mathsf T},
 &\mathbb E\widehat Q_2
 &=-\int_Dv\Delta_e\Pi_k(e^*v^{\mathsf T}),\\
 \mathbb E\widehat R_1
 &=R+\int_Dv\Delta_e(\Delta_0+e^*\tau^*),
 &\mathbb E\widehat R_2
 &=-\int_Dv\Delta_e\Pi_k(\Delta_0+e^*\tau^*).
\end{aligned}
 \tag{12}
\]
For example, the first vector identity follows from
\[
 \mathbb E[(Y-\bar\mu)(A-\bar e)\mid X=x]
 =e(x)\{1-e(x)\}\tau(x)
 +\{e(x)-\bar e\}\{\mu_0(x)-\bar\mu+e(x)\tau(x)\},
\]
and the second-order identities follow from independence of the two observations and the exact Gram (3).  Let \(\widehat S=\widehat R-\widehat Q\theta\).  Since \(R-Q\theta=0\), subtraction in (12) gives, component by component,
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat S_a
 =\int_D v_a\Delta_e(I-\Pi_k)
 \{\Delta_0+e^*(\tau^*-\tau_h^*)\}.
\]
Self-adjointness and idempotence of the exact orthogonal projection turn this into
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat S_a
 =\left\langle(I-\Pi_k)(v_a\Delta_e),
 (I-\Pi_k)\{\Delta_0+e^*(\tau^*-\tau_h^*)\}\right\rangle_{L_2(D)}.
 \tag{13}
\]
By (4), (7), \(e^*\leq1/2\), and the contraction property of \(I-\Pi_k\),
\[
 \|\mathbb E\widehat S\|
 \leq C\ell^\alpha(\ell^\beta+h^\gamma)
 =C\{\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
This derives separately the nuisance-product term and the interaction between propensity approximation and contrast smoothing.

We also need stabilization, and do not assume it.  From (12),
\[
 B_Q:=\mathbb E\widehat Q-Q
 =\int_Dv\Delta_e(I-\Pi_k)(e^*v^{\mathsf T}).
\]
For unit vectors \(a,c\), projection orthogonality and (1)--(2) give
\[
 |a^{\mathsf T}B_Qc|
 \leq\|(a^{\mathsf T}v)\Delta_e\|_2
       \|e^*(c^{\mathsf T}v)\|_2
 \leq\frac18\cdot\frac12=\frac1{16}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Combining (6) and (15) yields
\[
 s_{\min}(\mathbb E\widehat Q)\geq1/8.
 \tag{16}
\]

It remains to derive the stochastic terms.  The first-order summands in both \(\widehat S\) and \(\widehat Q\) are bounded multiples of \(K_h(X)\), so uniform design gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|H_1(O)\|^2\leq C\int_{D_h}h^{-2d}\,dx=Ch^{-d}.
 \tag{17}
\]
For the second-order summands, orthonormality in (3) gives the exact Hilbert--Schmidt calculation
\[
 \int_D\!\int_D\{b_k(z_1)^{\mathsf T}b_k(z_2)\}^2,dz_1dz_2
 =\operatorname{tr}(\Omega_k^2)=k.
\]
After the two changes of variables \(x_j=hz_j\), this implies
\[
 \mathbb E\|H_2(O_1,O_2)\|^2\leq Ckh^{-2d}.
 \tag{18}
\]
The first conditional projection of \(H_2\) has squared norm at most \(Ch^{-d}\): conditional expectation integrates one copy of \(b_k\), and the resulting \(\Pi_k\)-term is bounded in \(L_2(D)\) by orthogonal-projection contraction; the remaining outer localization contributes \(h^{-d}\), exactly as in (17).  The same bound holds after interchanging the observations.

For completeness, symmetrize the possibly nonsymmetric kernel by replacing \(H_2(o_1,o_2)\) with \(\{H_2(o_1,o_2)+H_2(o_2,o_1)\}/2\), and incorporate \(H_1\) as \(\{H_1(o_1)+H_1(o_2)\}/2\).  The resulting unordered U-statistic is exactly the sum of the empirical and ordered-U terms in (9).  If \(H^\circ=H-\mathbb EH-H_1^\circ(o_1)-H_1^\circ(o_2)\), direct expansion shows that the three summands are pairwise orthogonal and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathbb U_nH)
 =\frac4n\mathbb E\|H_1^\circ(O)\|^2
 +\frac2{n(n-1)}\mathbb E\|H^\circ(O_1,O_2)\|^2.
\]
Using (17)--(18), and summing the fixed number of vector or matrix coordinates, proves
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat S-\mathbb E\widehat S\|^2
 +\mathbb E\|\widehat Q-\mathbb E\widehat Q\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 \leq C W_{n,h,k},
 \qquad
 W_{n,h,k}=\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{n^2h^{2d}}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Thus \((nh^d)^{-1/2}\) is the nondegenerate empirical scale and \(\sqrt{k}/(nh^d)\) is the degenerate projection scale; neither has been suppressed.

Let \(\mathcal G=\{\|\widehat Q-\mathbb E\widehat Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1/16\}\).  Equations (16) and (19), Chebyshev's inequality when \(W_{n,h,k}\leq1\), and the trivial probability bound otherwise give
\[
 \mathbb P(\mathcal G^c)\leq C\min\{1,W_{n,h,k}\}
 \leq C\sqrt{W_{n,h,k}}.
 \tag{20}
\]
On \(\mathcal G\), the least singular value of \(\widehat Q\) exceeds \(1/16\), so the flooring in (10) is inactive and \(\|\widehat Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq16\).  Since clipping cannot increase distance from \(\tau(0)\in[-3/4,3/4]\), (7), (14), (19), and (20) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E|\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau(0)|
 &\leq Ch^\gamma+C\mathbb E\{\|\widehat S\|{\bf1}_{\mathcal G}\}
      +\frac32\mathbb P(\mathcal G^c)\\
 &\leq C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha
 +\sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}+\frac{k}{n^2h^{2d}}}\right\}\\
 &=C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha
 +\sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, successive admissible dimensions have bounded ratio, so replacing an arbitrary target dimension by a nearest admissible one changes \(\ell\), \(k\), and the bound only by fixed constants.  This proves the claim for every \(n\geq2\), including the cases in which a variance term exceeds one.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\kappa=0\), put \(S=\alpha+\beta\), and define
\[
 S_\star=\frac{d\gamma}{2\gamma+d},
 \qquad
 D_\star=1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2S}.
\]
Then every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) satisfies
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
There are constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that for every \(n\geq2\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by a total one-sided localized second-order projection R-learner.  In particular, if \(S\geq S_\star\), then
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
There is no logarithmic multiplier at \(S=S_\star\): at that equality the two finite bias--variance balances coincide.  If \(S<S_\star\), the result asserts the displayed bracket with upper rate \(n^{-1/D_\star}\) but does not assert a matching nuisance-dominated lower bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  The definition of \(r_\kappa\), \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}shape}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\mbox{-}envelope}\) give, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
 e_P(x)=\frac{r_0(x)g_P(x)}4=\frac{g_P(x)}4,
 \qquad
 \frac14\leq e_P(x)\leq\frac12.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus this is the same exact-uniform class with bounded overlap, not a restricted submodel.

For the lower bound, any data-only Borel estimator \(T\) induces the supplied-propensity estimator \(T^e(o_{1:n},e)=T(o_{1:n})\), which ignores its second argument.  By \(\mathrm{def:unknown\mbox{-}risk}\) and \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}risk}\),
\[
 R_n^e(d,0,\beta,\gamma,L)leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L).
 \tag{2}
\]
The lower half of \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\), specialized to \(\kappa=0\), and (2) imply
\[
 c_e n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \tag{3}
\]
for every \(n\geq2\).  This is a supplied-propensity lower bound on the same uniform-design Bernoulli class.

For the upper bound, invoke \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\).  Since \(\ell\leq1\), its interaction term satisfies \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\leq h^\gamma\).  Hence its explicit data-only estimator obeys
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau_P(0)|
 \leq C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+(nh^d)^{-1/2}
 +\frac{\sqrt{k}}{nh^d}\right\}.
 \tag{4}
\]

First suppose \(S<S_\star\).  Set \(\delta=D_\star^{-1}\), and choose, up to the bounded admissible-rank rounding in the lemma,
\[
 h=n^{-1/(\gamma D_\star)}=n^{-\delta/\gamma},
 \qquad
 k\asymp n^{(d/S-d/\gamma)/D_\star}
 =n^{\delta d(1/S-1/\gamma)}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Here \(S<S_\star<\gamma\), so the exponent of \(k\) is positive.  Equations (5) give
\[
 \ell=h k^{-1/d}\asymp n^{-\delta/S},
 \qquad
 h^\gamma\asymp\ell^S\asymp n^{-\delta}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Moreover, using \(1=\delta\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{k}}{nh^d}
 \asymp n^{-1+\delta d/(2S)+\delta d/(2\gamma)}
 =n^{-\delta}.
 \tag{7}
\]
The exponent of the nondegenerate term is
\[
 \frac12-\frac{\delta d}{2\gamma},
\]
and its excess over \(\delta\) equals
\[
 \left(\frac12-\frac{\delta d}{2\gamma}\right)-\delta
 =\frac{d(1/S-1/\gamma)-2}{4D_\star}\geq0,
 \tag{8}
\]
where the last inequality is equivalent to \(S\leq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)=S_\star\).  Substitution of (6)--(8) into (4) proves
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\leq Cn^{-1/D_\star}
 \qquad(S<S_\star).
 \tag{9}
\]

Now suppose \(S\geq S_\star\).  Choose
\[
 h=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 k\asymp nh^d.
 \tag{10}
\]
Then
\[
 h^\gamma=(nh^d)^{-1/2}asymp\frac{\sqrt{k}}{nh^d}
 =n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 \ell\asymp n^{-1/d}.
 \tag{11}
\]
The definition of \(S_\star\) is exactly the equivalence
\[
 S\geq S_\star
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac Sd\geq\frac\gamma{2\gamma+d},
\]
so (11) gives
\[
 \ell^S\lesssim n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Equations (4) and (10)--(12) prove the oracle upper rate throughout \(S\geq S_\star\).  At \(S=S_\star\), (12) is an equality of powers, and (8) is also an equality: the local-polynomial bias, projection bias, nondegenerate variance, and degenerate variance are a finite collection of terms of the same pure-power order.  No dyadic or harmonic sum occurs, so no logarithmic multiplier is introduced.

Finally, \(D_\star^{-1}\leq\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) exactly when \(S\leq S_\star\).  Therefore (9) and the high-smoothness upper bound combine as
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.
\]
Together with (3), this proves the bracket and the matching conclusion for \(S\geq S_\star\).  Below the elbow, only the upper side has been improved; no nuisance-dominated converse is inferred.
added_lemmas.justification: On the exact-uniform bounded-overlap slice, the known design makes the localized projection Gram exact.  A total second-order R-learner therefore improves the all-regime upper bound and proves oracle-rate attainment under the sharp upper-side threshold \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).
added_lemmas.gap: When \(\alpha+\beta<d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), the exact-uniform class still lacks a matching nuisance-dominated product-mixture lower bound, so the improved upper rate is not claimed minimax sharp.
added_lemmas.consumer: For a fixed uniform design with bounded overlap, local-CATE users now have a total computable estimator and the oracle rate under the weaker nuisance-sum threshold; below that threshold they have an explicit improved upper precision guarantee without an unsupported claim about causal forests.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former theorem is a strictly weaker first-order bracket.  The replacement proves the directed second-order upper bound and expands the certified oracle-rate slice while preserving the same exact model class; deletion with replacement migrates its inbound frontier dependency atomically.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The causal target is \(\tau_P(0)\); it is not defined by an estimator.  For general \(\kappa\ge0\), the established data-only map \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), gives \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\]  On the bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), the total data-only map \(\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) satisfies, for \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(\ell=hk^{-1/d}\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\le C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha+\sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)}\right\}.\]  With \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\), its optimized consequence is \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\le C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.\]  Hence the unknown- and supplied-propensity risks have the same rate whenever \(S\ge S_\star\), including equality without a logarithm.  For \(S<S_\star\), the matching exact-uniform lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the sharper higher-order frontier beyond the first-order bracket remains open.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior functional advertised only the first-order estimator and the stronger sufficient condition \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  The proved second-order map, its optimized bounded-overlap rate, and the remaining lower-bound and corner-zero gaps must be stated separately from the causal target.

proposed.comparator_claim: Definition 2 and equation (14) give a localized higher-order polynomial R-learner and the bounded-overlap upper balance; Theorems 1--2 pair it with a lower construction over a density-qualified design class whose displayed witness has perforated support.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper is now proved on the exact uniform design and is informed by the cited KBRW and HOIF constructions, while the KBRW nuisance-dominated lower witness still does not transfer to the singleton uniform design.

prose_updates.tldr: For the full exact local-zero model, the proved supplied-propensity lower bound and total first-order estimator give \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  On the exact-uniform bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), a total second-order projection R-learner improves the upper bound to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]}\}\).  It proves the oracle rate once \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithm at equality.  The nuisance-dominated exact-uniform converse below that elbow and the sharper \(\kappa>0\) frontier remain open.

project_justification.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE proves the bounded-overlap contrast frontier over a density-qualified design class, but its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  Its lower witness therefore does not establish the nuisance-dominated converse on the singleton uniform design, and no current result supplies the full corner-zero frontier for \(\kappa>0\).
project_justification.niche: Exact knowledge of the uniform covariate law makes the localized projection Gram deterministic.  This permits a one-sided second-order R-learner on the full uniform cube, isolating the upper-side nuisance elbow without a covariate-density estimation remainder, while the local-zero geometry remains available for the unresolved weak-overlap problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives a total finite-operation second-order estimator on \(\kappa=0\) with risk \(h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha+\sqrt{(nh^d)^{-1}\{1+k/(nh^d)\}}\).  Optimizing it yields the bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\le R_n\le C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]}\}\) and the exact oracle rate above the elbow.  The paper does not claim the missing lower side below the elbow or a solved higher-order \(\kappa>0\) frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Definition 2 and equation (14), supplies the bounded-overlap higher-order local-polynomial architecture adapted here.  Theorem 3 derives its one-sided exact-uniform analogue with an exact Lebesgue Gram and bounded deterministic pilots.  Their Theorems 1--2 and Definition 1 give the closest full pointwise contrast frontier, but the displayed perforated-support lower witness does not prove the nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform design.  Consequently the present high-smoothness match uses Theorem 1's exact-uniform supplied-propensity lower bound, while the below-elbow converse remains open.  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies first-order local-polynomial R-learner motivation, and LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
prose_updates.interpretation: At bounded overlap with a known uniform design, pointwise CATE estimation reaches supplied-propensity precision as soon as the combined propensity and control smoothness satisfies \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), a strictly weaker sufficient condition than \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  Below this elbow, the second-order estimator gives a faster certified upper bound, but the absence of a same-class nuisance lower experiment means that an information-theoretic cost of unknown propensity has not yet been proved.  These are minimax statements about local CATE precision, not attainment guarantees for an existing forest implementation.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper inequality is now closed, but its rough-nuisance converse is not.  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\) violate the \(\gamma\)-H\"older bound below the elbow; overlapping smooth squared frames repair transition regularity but fall outside the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and retain shared-sign cross terms in fixed-\(n\) product mixtures.  Filling perforated transition holes directly contributes order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which is too large at the proposed nuisance separation.  For \(\kappa>0\), estimated-score variance, noninteger corner powers, and max-norm tie surfaces still require separate upper and lower repairs.
prose_updates.honest_scope: For arbitrary \(\kappa\ge0\), the established statement remains the first-order bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  On \(\kappa=0\), the proved second-order estimator improves the upper exponent to \(1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]\) below the elbow and attains \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) when \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  The equality case has no logarithm because four finite balance terms have the same power.  No nuisance-dominated lower bound is claimed below the elbow, so whether unknown \(g_P\) changes the minimax rate there remains open; the full higher-order and critical-log frontier for \(\kappa>0\) also remains open.

statement_notes.justification: Known uniform design makes the localized projection Gram exact, allowing a total second-order R-learner to establish the strongest proved bounded-overlap upper frontier on the same model class.
statement_notes.gap: Below \(\alpha+\beta=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), the exact-uniform full-support product-mixture lower bound is still missing, so only the displayed bracket is certified.
statement_notes.consumer: Researchers using fixed uniform bounded-overlap designs obtain the oracle pointwise CATE rate under the weaker combined-smoothness threshold and an explicit improved upper rate below it, without attributing the result to an unmodified causal forest.
